page_title: AI Access Auditor: see and control what your AI agents can do

sources.entry: AI Access Auditor - See and revoke what AI coding agents like Claude Code, Codex and Cursor can access on your Mac. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/dirmedmr-alt/ai-access-auditor) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: AI Access Auditor
summary.one_liner: A free desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux that shows every permission, folder, login and key your AI coding agents have, and lets you revoke them.
keywords: see what ai agents can access
stop ai agent from running commands
use_cases: Audit what Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI can access on your computer
Approve or deny agent shell commands and file changes before they run
Revoke stale AI agent permissions, trusted folders or MCP servers
Detect AI agents started in YOLO or root mode
Monitor whether a script started by an agent is sending data out
summary.what_it_does: The app inventories AI agent access on the machine, including tool permissions, trusted folders, MCP servers, agent skills, saved logins (such as sudo, SSH, GitHub, AWS, gcloud and Kubernetes), browser and editor extensions, background jobs and macOS privacy permissions. A menu bar shield watches agent settings and processes and shows a popup when access changes. For Claude Code, Codex CLI and Gemini CLI it can show Allow/Deny prompts before actions run, if "Ask before it acts" is enabled. Each grant has a risk level and a one-line explanation, and changes can be removed with one click, after a backup, and restored from History. Temporary grants can be set for an hour, a day or a week.
notable: Pre-action Allow/Deny popups for Claude Code, Codex CLI and Gemini CLI, including YOLO mode
Reverts changes from a backup history
Open source, with no account and no tracking inside the app
caveats: Windows build is not code-signed yet, so Windows shows a warning on install; Windows on ARM is untested
Cannot block individual network connections; it stops the sending program instead and checks every 2 seconds, so very short uploads may be missed
Reading macOS system permissions requires Full Disk Access; without it those items are not included
A team/company version is only planned, not available
